result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.birank()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Rank the nodes of a bipartite graph with BiRank. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L12165-L12322){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.birank( top_nodes, alpha=None, beta=None, top_personalization=None, bottom_personalization=None, max_iter=100, tol=1e-06, weighted=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![BiRank](/assets/graphs/birank.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Customers ann, cy and bob on top and products jam, tea and bread below, every node shaded by its BiRank score; each side sums to 1. tea, bought by all three, is the top product at 0.464, ahead of jam and bread at 0.268, and ann and bob, who bought tea plus one more, lead the customers at 0.369, ahead of cy at 0.261." width="100%"} BiRank (He et al., 2017) ranks both sides of a bipartite network at once, in the spirit of PageRank: a node is important when it is connected to important nodes on the other side, with each edge's influence normalized by both endpoints' degrees so that hubs do not dominate. Optional personalization vectors pull the ranking toward a query, which makes it a recommendation method: ranking products for a customer, papers for an author, or drugs for a disease. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [top_nodes]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[Union[int, str]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The nodes on one side (IDs or labels); every other node is on the bottom side. [alpha]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : How much the top (`alpha`) and bottom (`beta`) scores follow the propagated scores versus the personalization, between 0 and 1. Default 0.8 for a side with personalization, otherwise 1. [beta]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : How much the top (`alpha`) and bottom (`beta`) scores follow the propagated scores versus the personalization, between 0 and 1. Default 0.8 for a side with personalization, otherwise 1. [top_personalization]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [dict | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional dictionaries of non-negative query weights, keyed by node ID or label. [bottom_personalization]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [dict | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional dictionaries of non-negative query weights, keyed by node ID or label. [max_iter]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[100]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Maximum number of iterations (default 100). [tol]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1e-06]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Convergence tolerance (default `1e-6`). [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to use edge weights. If `None` (default), follows the graph's `weighted` flag. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict[int, float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Node ID to score, for both sides. Without personalization, each side's scores sum to 1. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If a side is empty, `alpha` or `beta` is outside $[0, 1]$, a personalization value is negative, a node does not exist, or the iteration does not converge. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} With the bottom-by-top weight matrix $W$ and $S = D_u^{-1/2} W D_p^{-1/2}$, the scores alternate $p \leftarrow \alpha S^\top u + (1 - \alpha) p_0$ and $u \leftarrow \beta S p + (1 - \beta) u_0$ from a uniform $p$, until both change by less than the tolerance; without personalization the result is normalized to sum 1 per side. This is NetworkX's `bipartite.birank`, step for step. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Customers and the products they bought: the most popular product, and the customer who bought popular products, rank highest: ::: {#198ede7e .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph().add_nodes(["ann", "bob", "cy", "tea", "jam", "bread"]) g.add_edges( [("ann", "tea"), ("ann", "jam"), ("bob", "tea"), ("bob", "bread"), ("cy", "tea")] ) scores = g.birank(top_nodes=["ann", "bob", "cy"]) {g.get_label_from_id(n): round(s, 3) for n, s in scores.items()} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {'ann': 0.369, 'bob': 0.369, 'cy': 0.261, 'tea': 0.464, 'jam': 0.268, 'bread': 0.268} ``` ::: :::
